context: You will hear two university students, Maya and Leo, discussing a research project on food waste.

script.t: Hi Maya. Have you got a few minutes to talk about our project on food waste? The proposal's due on Friday.
Sure. I've been thinking about how we collect the data. I know we said we'd use a questionnaire, but I'm not sure students will tell us honestly how much food they throw away.
That's true. People tend to underestimate it. What about weighing the waste instead?
That's what I was going to suggest. If the canteen manager agrees, we could weigh what's left on the plates at lunchtime for two weeks.
Two weeks seems long. Couldn't we do one?
Our tutor said that one week wouldn't be enough to see any pattern, because menus change from day to day. So I think we need two.
Fair enough. And we could still do a short questionnaire to find out why people leave food.
Yes, that would give us the reasons, not just the amounts. Now, about the literature review. I've found three sources so far.
Go on.
The first is a government report from 2019. It's got lots of national statistics, but it's quite general; it doesn't say much about universities.
We could still use it in the introduction to show the scale of the problem.
Exactly. The second is a journal article by Hansen about a university in Denmark. It's very relevant, but the sample was small, only about two hundred students.
That's still useful, as long as we mention the limitation. What's the third?
A book by Clarke. It's really well written, but it was published in 1998, so a lot of the data is out of date.
Hmm. I'd only use it for the theory, then, not the figures.
Agreed. Now, how should we divide the work? I'm happy to contact the canteen manager, since I know her a bit already.
Great. Then I'll design the questionnaire. I did something similar last year.
And what about analysing the data? Neither of us is very confident with statistics.
Why don't we ask Dr Okafor for help? She runs a statistics workshop on Wednesdays.
Good idea. One more thing: what do you think the biggest challenge will be?
Honestly, for me it'll be getting enough students to complete the questionnaire. Response rates are always low at the end of term.
And for me, it's time. Weighing the waste every day is going to take a lot of effort, and we've both got exams coming.

questions.prompt: Why does Maya want to weigh food waste rather than rely only on a questionnaire?
options: Students may not report their waste accurately.
Questionnaires take too long to analyse.
The canteen manager asked them to.
questions.quote: I'm not sure students will tell us honestly how much food they throw away

questions.prompt: Why do they decide to collect data for two weeks?
options: The canteen is closed on some days.
Menus vary from day to day.
Leo has more free time in the second week.
questions.quote: because menus change from day to day
questions.explain: "vary" = **change**. Leo bir hafta önerdi ama hoca menülerin değiştiğini söyledi.

questions.prompt: What will the questionnaire be used for?
options: to measure the amount of waste
to find out why students leave food
questions.quote: to find out why people leave food
questions.explain: Anket **nedenleri** bulmak için; miktar tartılarak ölçülecek.
